claims.text: Laser power, scanning speed, and powder feed rate are relevant controllable parameters for additive processing of high-entropy alloys.
Optimizing laser power, scanning speed, and powder feed rate can improve dimensional precision in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Optimizing laser power, scanning speed, and powder feed rate can improve mechanical integrity in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Optimizing laser power, scanning speed, and powder feed rate can reduce fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Powder feed rate influences microhardness, laser power influences dilution rate, and scanning speed influences aspect ratio during laser cladding of AlCoCrFeNi.
Control of the selected process parameters can optimize the alloy microstructure.
Control of the selected process parameters can minimize defect formation.
The resulting changes in microstructure and defect formation will improve dimensional precision.
The resulting changes in microstructure and defect formation will improve mechanical integrity.
Dimensional precision and mechanical integrity will improve by 10–20% relative to the current fabrication baseline.
The predicted effect applies generally to additive manufacturing with optimized process parameters.
The exact relationship between process parameters and defect formation is not fully understood.
The relationship between process parameters and defect formation may vary with the specific high-entropy alloy.
Failure to achieve at least a 5% improvement in both dimensional precision and mechanical integrity relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 10–20% improvement, but the falsification rule only rejects improvements below 5%. An outcome between 5% and 10% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
